response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT o.timespan, AVG(f.rebrate / NULLIF(f.feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio, COUNT(*) AS match_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), a AS (SELECT AVG(match_count) AS avg_cnt FROM g) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS avg_of_avg_ratios, SUM(g.match_count) AS total_match_count, AVG(g.match_count - a.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess_over_average FROM g CROSS JOIN a WHERE g.match_count > a.avg_cnt

assumptions.assumption: Match count is the number of joined fee-order rows per timespan group (COUNT(*)), and the cross-group average is the plain average of those group counts.
A feerate of 0 makes the ratio undefined, so it is treated as missing (NULLIF) and ignored in the average, which also avoids a division-by-zero error.
An order with a NULL timespan, if any exist, forms its own group and counts as a group in the cross-group average.
